pins.label: A7

pins.notes: Also wired to the empty SPI flash footprint U3 on the back (only matters if you solder a flash chip). 5 V tolerant only as a digital input. As an analog input keep it between 0 and 3.3 V.

pins.notes: 5 V tolerant only as a digital input. As an analog input keep it between 0 and 3.3 V.

pins.notes: 5 V tolerant only as a digital input. As an analog input keep it between 0 and 3.3 V.

pins.notes: 5 V tolerant only as a digital input. As an analog input keep it between 0 and 3.3 V.

pins.label: C15

pins.label: C14
pins.notes: 32.768 kHz crystal pin. Leave it free.

i2c.note: Only certain pin pairs can be I2C on this chip, and SDA and SCL cannot be swapped in software. Wire uses GP4 (SDA) and GP5 (SCL); Wire.setSDA()/Wire.setSCL() before Wire.begin() can move I2C0 to GP0/GP1, GP8/GP9, GP12/GP13, GP16/GP17 or GP20/GP21. Wire1 defaults to GP26/GP27.

boards.name: Teensy 4.1
boards.cpu: Arm Cortex-M7 at 600 MHz, 1024 KB RAM, 8 MB flash, native USB
boards.summary: A very fast (600 MHz) breadboard-friendly board with native USB, lots of serial, I2C and SPI ports and a microSD slot. 3.3 V logic; the pins are not 5 V tolerant.

pins.label: 5V
pins.notes: VIN (printed 5V): 5 V from USB when plugged in. Can also take 3.6 to 5.5 V input; cut the VUSB-VIN pad before using external power together with USB.

pins.label: 3V
pins.notes: 3.3 V output from the on-board regulator (250 mA max for everything you connect).
Default I2C clock (Wire SCL). Also analog A5.
Default I2C data (Wire SDA). Also analog A4.
Orange on-board LED, and also the SPI clock (SCK). HIGH turns the LED on.
Serial1 RX. The USB serial monitor does not use this pin (Teensy has native USB).
Serial1 TX. The USB serial monitor does not use this pin (Teensy has native USB).

pins.label: 3V
pins.notes: 3.3 V output from the on-board regulator (250 mA max for everything you connect).

pins.label: On/Off
pins.notes: Power control: a button from here to GND held 4 s turns the 3.3 V power off, 0.5 s turns it back on.

pins.label: Program
pins.notes: Pulling this to GND does the same as the white button: enters programming mode. It is not a reset.

pins.label: 3.3V
pins.notes: 3.3 V output from the on-board regulator (250 mA max for everything you connect).

pins.label: VBAT
pins.notes: Input for a 3 V coin cell (CR2032) to keep the real-time clock running. It does not supply power to parts.

i2c.note: Wire only works on pins 18 (SDA) and 19 (SCL). Wire1 uses 17 (SDA1) and 16 (SCL1); Wire2 uses 25 (SDA2) and 24 (SCL2).
